items.text: AMEND (T) AND RECOMMIT TO ENERGY AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS
COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to requiring the emergency
response plan of an electric corporation to include plans for how the
communication and coordination of efforts shall occur
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S932

SPONSOR: KAPLAN
 
PURPOSE:

This legislation will require electric corporations in their emergency
response plans to include how communication and coordination of efforts
between the electric corporation, electric corporation employees, elec-
tric corporation company crews, mutual aid crews, local governments,
television providers, internet providers, and any other entity perform-
ing services to assist such electric corporation shall occur.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Paragraph (a) of subdivision 21 of section 66 of the public
service law, is amended to require electric corporations in their emer-
gency response plans to include how communication and coordination of
efforts between the electric corporation, electric corporation employ-
ees, electric corporation company crews, mutual aid crews, local govern-
ments, television providers, internet providers, and any other entity
performing services to assist such electric corporation shall occur.

Section 2 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

During Tropical Storm Isaias many impacted individuals, as well as many
crews responding to the storm expressed a frustration in the communi-
cation that was occurring between the various entities that were
responding to the storm. It was a common occurrence that crews would
show up prepared to fix downed lines, or trim downed trees, only to find
themselves unable to complete their work as they waited for another crew
to perform work that was necessary before they could undertake their own
work. Workers could spend hours waiting, hoping that assistance would
show up and only be ultimately be frustrated when that never occurred.
These crews expressed a frustration as they had no ability to find out
when or if assistance would be coming. This legislation attempts to get
electric corporations to come up and submit a plan for review on how
conversations between all those performing work will occur. It is also
through better coordination of all services that residents rely on that
the repair of electric, phone, cable, and internet lines can be done in
a more efficient manner. It is the hope that by putting together a writ-
ten plan that must be reviewed that communication will improve, and as a
result storm responses will al so be improved.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S. 8929/A. 11015; Referred to Senate Rules Committee

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

BILL NUMBER: S932A

SPONSOR: KAPLAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public service law and the public authorities law,
in relation to requiring the emergency response plan of an electric
corporation to include plans for how the communication and coordination
of efforts shall occur

 
PURPOSE:

This legislation will require electric corporations, as well as LIPA in
their emergency response plans to include how communication and coordi-
nation of efforts between the electric corporation, electric corporation
employees, electric corporation company crews, mutual aid crews, other
utilities, local governments and any other entity performing services to
assist such electric corporation shall occur.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Paragraph (a) of subdivision 21 of section 66 of the public
service law, is amended to require electric corporations, in their emer-
gency response plans to include how communication and coordination of
efforts between the electric corporation, electric corporation employ-
ees, electric corporation company crews, mutual aid crews, other utili-
ties, local governments and any other entity performing services to
assist such electric corporation shall occur.

Section 2 require LIPA in their emergency response plans to include how
communication and coordination of efforts between LIPA, the service
provider, LIPA's employees, service provider employees, LIPA company
crews, service provider company crews, mutual aid crews, other utili-
ties, local governments and any other entity performing services to
assist such electric corporation shall occur.

Section 3 is the effective date.

During Tropical Storm Isaias many impacted individuals, as well as many

cation that was occurring between the various entities that were
responding to the storm. It was a common occurrence that crews would
show up prepared to fix downed lines, or trim downed trees, only to find
themselves unable to complete their work as they waited for another crew
to perform work that was necessary before they could undertake their own
work. Workers could spend hours waiting, hoping that assistance would
show up and only be ultimately be frustrated when that never occurred.
These crews expressed a frustration as they had no ability to find out
when or if assistance would be coming. This legislation attempts to get
electric corporations to come up and submit a plan for review on how
conversations between all those performing work will occur. It is also
through better coordination of all services that residents rely on that
the repair of electric, phone, cable, and internet lines can be done in
a more efficient manner. It is the hope that by putting together a writ-
ten plan that must be reviewed that communication will improve, and as a
result storm responses will al so be improved.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S.8929/A.11015; Referred to Senate Rules Committee

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Requires the emergency response plan of an electric corporation or the Long Island power authority to include plans for how the communication and coordination of efforts shall occur between the various parties involved in implementing such emergency response plan.
